text: An unpaid invoice isn't the end of the story — a payment eventually has to go out and be tracked against it. This lesson separates three ideas that get blurred together: the schedule of when a payment is expected, the actual application of a payment, and the physical payment document itself.

When an invoice is validated, Oracle Fusion calculates when it's due based on payment terms. That plan lives in AP_PAYMENT_SCHEDULES_ALL. Be precise here: a payment schedule is a plan. It exists the moment an invoice is validated, whether or not any money has moved yet.

Once a payment is actually made, the link to the invoices it settles lives in AP_INVOICE_PAYMENTS_ALL. This is many-to-many: one invoice can be paid across several payments over time, and one payment can cover several invoices at once. Each row records the amount applied in that specific pairing.

That table records that an invoice and a payment were linked — but the actual check number or EFT reference is generated through Oracle Payments, the I-B-Y module. That disbursement engine is shared across products, rather than Payables keeping its own private checks table the old way.

Keep these as three separate questions about the same invoice: scheduled, applied, and disbursed. An invoice can be fully scheduled but not applied, or applied but not finished disbursing. Collapsing all of that into one "is it paid" question produces wrong answers later. Up next, lesson ten: the receivables side of this same pattern.
